frase_gancho.texto: A quechquémitl where a four-petaled star blooms.

puente_narrativo.texto: From the garment, we move on to the festival that fills the region with flowers. Look for a great arch of rods covered in yellow flowers, and a table with bread, tamales, chocolate and candles.

guion_corto.texto: This quechquémitl, called dhúbem in the teenek language, is the formal garment of Huastec women in San Luis Potosí and Veracruz. It is made from two panels of white cotton cloth joined in a diamond shape, and covered with cross-stitch embroidery in wool of intense colors: magenta, orange, green, yellow and blue. Look at the design in the center: a flower with four petals, which is interpreted as the morning star, the four directions of the world and the tree of life. Women wear it at festivals, at weddings and during Xantolo, the celebration of the dead. It is a garment that speaks of continuity: the flower they embroider today was embroidered centuries ago.

guion_largo.texto:
If you have walked through the halls attentively, you already know some pieces from the Huastecs. In the Gulf Coast Hall you saw the sculpture of the [Adolescent of Tamuín](mna_s08_adolescente_huasteco), carved more than a thousand years ago by their ancestors. Here you see them alive: the teenek, who still live in the Huasteca, in San Luis Potosí, Veracruz and Hidalgo. And the quechquémitl in front of you is one of their most beautiful garments.

Before talking about embroidery, a linguistic surprise. The teenek language belongs to the Maya family, just like the Maya language of Yucatán and the languages of Chiapas. But the Huastecs live hundreds of kilometers from the Maya, on the Gulf Coast. Linguists estimate that their languages separated about three thousand years ago. It is as if, in a very remote time, a piece of the Maya family had traveled north and stayed there. Today, according to the censuses, more than one hundred thousand people speak teenek.

Now, the garment. The quechquémitl, like the Otomí one you already know, is made of two panels joined to form a diamond. But the teenek style is unmistakable: white cotton cloth and cross-stitch embroidery in wool of intense colors. The reds, pinks, oranges and greens shine against the light background with a joy that can be recognized from far away.

The center of the design is a flower with four petals. It is usually associated with the tree of life, with the four directions of the universe and with the morning star. Four directions, four petals, a cross: the same idea you saw in the four Voladores (Flyers), in the cross of the [Otomí oratory](mna_s15_oratorio_familiar) and in the directions of the Maya world. It appears in different places, with other names, but with a similar intention.

Teenek women complete the outfit with a headdress of colored yarn, woven into the hair, which can be seen as a crown. It is thought to symbolize fertility and abundance. Altogether, the teenek woman in her finest dress seems to walk dressed as a garden: embroidered flowers, flowers of wool, colors unlike those of any other corner of the country.

The music also belongs to the region. The Huastec huapango, with violin, jarana and quinta guitar, and that voice that suddenly rises into a falsetto, is one of the most recognizable sounds of Mexico. At festival dances, the women show off these quechquémitls while the dancers stamp on wooden platforms, which are made to resonate with their feet. The clothing and the music form a single whole.

Look closely at the embroidery. Each stitch is a small cross, and the cloth is covered cross after cross until the designs take shape. It is work done with patience and with a fixed gaze. Between one stitch and the next, the teenek woman thinks of the flowers her grandmother embroidered. The garment is a bridge between generations, and the flower with four petals, its signature.

texto: Find the four-petaled flower in the center of the embroidery
Count how many different colors of wool you can make out
Look at the cross-stitch: can you follow a row of stitches?

texto.Region: Huasteca of San Luis Potosí and Veracruz (Tancanhuitz, Tantoyuca)
texto.Technique/Material: Cotton woven on a backstrap loom, cross-stitch embroidery, and wool yarn
texto.Function: Ceremonial dress for special occasions, marker of community rank, and protection of identity

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Huastecs are a people with no connection to the Maya.
texto.respuesta: Reality: Their language, teenek, belongs to the Maya family, even though they live far from the Maya of the south. The languages separated about three thousand years ago.
